title: Anthropic's $2trn IPO faces a Wall Street reality check
source_used: The Times (headline and standfirst only; body paywalled); Reuters prospectus facts as relayed by the SMH and The Observer; Bloomberg timing as relayed by SMH
key_facts: The Times (3 Oct 2026) says the lossmaking company is seeking a listing bigger than SpaceX's even as its filing warns of the catastrophe its AI systems could unleash; the body is paywalled
Reuters, as relayed by the SMH and The Observer, reports Anthropic seeks a valuation above $2 trillion and a mid-November float (Bloomberg)
Anthropic's prospectus shows a 2025 net loss of about $42 billion, about $34 billion of it an accounting charge, and an operating loss of about $8 billion
47 percent of its customer sales came through Amazon and Google clouds; Broadcom agreed to lend up to $42 billion for infrastructure, which the filing flags as a potential conflict of interest
Its largest operating cost is a $1.25 billion a month deal for SpaceX's Colossus 1 data centre until May 2029
Follow-up: on 2 Oct Bloomberg reported Anthropic targets a mega-IPO before Thanksgiving; new today is the scepticism about the $2trn price
quote_evidence: The lossmaking tech company is seeking to put the SpaceX listing in the shade even as it warns of the catastrophe its AI systems could unleash

Details from Anthropic's IPO prospectus, leaked to Reuters this week, failed to ease concerns that frontier labs rely on patronage. It shows that 47% of its sales to customers came through cloud partners Amazon and Google.
why_it_matters_hint: The biggest AI listing yet is meeting doubts about whether a 2 trillion dollar price fits 8 billion of operating losses
event_date: Times article 3 Oct 2026; prospectus reporting earlier this week
